```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Distribution fits a 90-day window better. The Shopify App Store has built-in merchant discovery and self-serve installs. Idea B leans on SEO, which its own brief says rewards long-run moats, and on Product Hunt, which reportedly needs an audience the founder does not have.",
    "Idea A's demand evidence describes the job itself. A merchant says they want to know why customers buy or don't, and has already tried and dropped manual calls. Idea B's demand evidence is mostly complaints about Statuspage's price, a gap that cheaper and free alternatives already fill.",
    "The price floor is less brutal for A. Its free-tier competitors cap usage (50 responses, 100 responses, 200 orders), so a growing store eventually hits a paywall. Idea B's own brief says a new entrant is effectively selling against OneUptime's unlimited free public page.",
    "Idea A's sourced proof point shows larger economics. A solo founder reached about $125K MRR in this category. Idea B's best comparable, Instatus, reached about $10K MRR with growth of roughly $500/mo after years in market.",
    "Idea A's price hypothesis of $25–$49/mo is anchored to several live paid tiers (Fairing, Grapevine, Analyzify). Idea B's $9–$29/mo is squeezed by StillOnline at $9 and OneUptime at $0–$22."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's pricing-pain evidence is a Reddit thread title asking why the market leader charges $399/month. It shows frustration with Atlassian Statuspage, not willingness to pay a new vendor. The brief itself documents that the gap is already served by OneUptime's free tier, StillOnline at $9/mo, and Hyperping at $29/mo, and that Hyperping already runs the 'incumbent is overpriced' SEO angle.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate to low. Both niches are saturated, and both briefs argue persuasively against themselves. Idea A has two caveats. The Zigpoll figure is flagged as coming from a seed quote, and that same story says traction took two years, which undercuts the 90-day goal. A zero-review app also faces a real install barrier. The edge for A rests mainly on marketplace distribution and usage-capped free tiers, not on strong evidence that a new entrant can convert a paying customer quickly."
}
```
